contexts.text: Not to hear the lip of a companion () = that they are all discordant, or one against another; for it is not to acknowledge what another is saying, and in the internal sense, it is not to acknowledge what another is teaching, or his doctrine.
As soon as this common tie (among evil Spirits) is dissolved, one rushes on another, and then their delight consists in a companion torturing his companions.
Being forsaken by his companions, the Spirit fell into another state...
When they were called companions, it was not from the good of love, but from the truth of faith. Illustrated.
Hence it is evident that the Jews and Israelites called each other brethren, but their allies companions.

Because we shall lie hid a man from his companion () = separation relatively to those things which are of the Church... A man from his companion = those who are within the Church, and those who are without it.
He and his companion Hirah the Adullamite () = that he was still in falsity... When he is called his companion, it is signified that it was adjoined to him.
The men were amazed, everyone to his companion () = a change of everyone's state among themselves.
They said that they live in dark forests, where they dare not do any violence to their companions, for then their companions are allowed to treat them savagely...
It was a custom that when one sinned, all his companions were held to be guilty... But such a law is derived from Hell, for there all companions conspire together for evil...

Wherefore smitest thou thy companion? () = chiding, because one wanted to destroy the faith of another... A companion = one who is in the truth of faith. He is called a companion, and not a brother, although they were both Hebrews, because they were enemies.
He comes to me, and I judge between a man and his companion () = that they are then arranged by revealed truth... To judge between a man and his companion = arrangement among truths.
He had taken something from his companion...
When a man's ox shall strike the ox of his companion () = two truths of which the affections are different, and that of one shall injure that of the other... A man and a companion = two truths.

When a man shall give to his companion silver or vessels to keep () = truths from good and corresponding scientifics in the memory... Two truths, as truth and the corresponding scientific, are in man a man and a companion.

Slay ye a man his brother, and a man his companion, and a man his neighbour () = a closing up as to the influx of good and truth, and of things related to them... Brother = the good of love and of charity; companion = the truth of that good; and neighbour = that which is conjoined with them, thus what is related.
With companions they never act from an evil end...
Companion is predicated of truth.
I John who am your brother and companion () = those who are in the good of charity, and thence in the truths of faith. Illustrated. AE 47, Explained.
As charity is that from which faith is derived, the Lord calls none companions, but brethren, or the neighbour.
An evil Spirit chooses companions with whom he lives in his own delight.
A female companion () = those who are in the goods of the Church.

They shall fight a man against his brother, and a man against his companion ()... By brother, and companion are signified the good from which is truth, and the truth from good; but in the opposite sense, the evil from which is falsity, and the falsity from evil. Illustrated.
